title: Tale of the Devotee Wrongly Accused (Português)

keywords: tale of the devotee wrongly accused
full_text:
An elderly hermit who had spent forty years tending a mountain shrine in Syria was framed by a corrupt tax-collector who had stolen a jeweled gold chalice from the municipal sanctuary. The tax-collector hid the chalice in the hermit’s cave, brought the guards, and accused the saintly elder of theft!

The mob gathered, ready to stone the hermit.

The old man stood with serene composure, looking at his accuser: 'If I am guilty, let the earth swallow me; but if I am innocent, let the chalice itself speak before this assembly!'

At that moment, the governor’s young son, who was playing with a hunting falcon nearby, stepped forward. The boy testified: 'Yesterday at sunset, while searching for my falcon, I saw this tax-collector climb the mountain path carrying a heavy sack under his cloak and enter the cave alone!'

The guards searched the tax-collector’s mule-bags and discovered the melted silver and jewels of other plundered shrines!

The corrupt official fell to his knees in terror, confessing his conspiracy.

The governor exonerated the saintly hermit with royal honors, punished the corrupt official, and rebuilt the mountain shrine, proving that an innocent life lived in truth is guarded by providence.
moral: Divine truth protects the innocent, and false accusations are dissolved by the light of evidence. [PT]
